text_en: Better is a dry morsel with quiet than a house full of feasting with strife.
text_cn: 干饼一张而平安共食，胜于满屋佳肴而互相争吵。

text_en: A slave who deals wisely will rule over a child who acts shamefully, and will share the inheritance as one of the family.
text_cn: 聪明的仆人必能管治任性的儿子，且可与弟兄们共分产业。

text_en: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace is for gold, but the Lord tests the heart.
text_cn: 锅炼银，炉炼金，上主炼人心。

text_en: An evildoer listens to wicked lips; and a liar gives heed to a mischievous tongue.
text_cn: 奸诈的人，爱听胡言乱语；说谎的人，轻信是非长短。

text_en: Those who mock the poor insult their Maker; those who are glad at calamity will not go unpunished.
text_cn: 嘲笑穷人的，是凌辱他的造主；幸灾乐祸的，必不能脱免惩罚。

text_en: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of children is their parents.
text_cn: 孙儿是老人的冠冕，父亲是儿女的光荣。

text_en: Fine speech is not becoming to a fool; still less is false speech to a ruler.
text_cn: 优雅的言词，不适宜于愚人；虚伪的狂语，更不宜于君王。

text_en: A bribe is like a magic stone in the eyes of those who give it; wherever they turn they prosper.
text_cn: 贿赂在馈赠者眼中，有如宝石；不论他要转向何方，无往不利。

text_en: One who forgives an affront fosters friendship, but one who dwells on disputes will alienate a friend.
text_cn: 掩饰他人的过错，可获得友爱；屡念旧日的过恶，则离间友谊。

text_en: A rebuke strikes deeper into a discerning person than a hundred blows into a fool.
text_cn: 对明智人一句指责，胜过对愚昧人百次杖击。

text_en: Evil people seek only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against them.
text_cn: 暴徒只求叛乱，但有残酷使者，奉命前来对付。

text_en: Better to meet a she-bear robbed of its cubs than to confront a fool immersed in folly.
text_cn: 宁愿遇见失掉幼子的母熊，不愿逢着正在发狂的愚人。

text_en: Evil will not depart from the house of one who returns evil for good.
text_cn: 谁以怨报德，灾祸必不离开他的家。

text_en: The beginning of strife is like letting out water; so stop before the quarrel breaks out.
text_cn: 争论的开端，如水之破堤；在激辩之前，应极加制止。

text_en: One who justifies the wicked and one who condemns the righteous are both alike an abomination to the Lord .
text_cn: 宣判罪人无罪，判定义人有罪：二者同为上主所憎恶。

text_en: Why should fools have a price in hand to buy wisdom, when they have no mind to learn?
text_cn: 愚昧的人，既没有头脑，手执金钱买智慧，又何益之有？

text_en: A friend loves at all times, and kinsfolk are born to share adversity.
text_cn: 朋友平时常相爱，唯在难中见兄弟。

text_en: It is senseless to give a pledge, to become surety for a neighbor.
text_cn: 常为人击掌作保，实是个无知之徒。

text_en: One who loves transgression loves strife; one who builds a high threshold invites broken bones.
text_cn: 好争辩的人，实喜爱罪过；高举门户的，必自趋灭亡。

text_en: The crooked of mind do not prosper, and the perverse of tongue fall into calamity.
text_cn: 谁存心欺诈，不会得幸福；谁搬弄是非，必陷于灾祸。

text_en: The one who begets a fool gets trouble; the parent of a fool has no joy.
text_cn: 生糊涂孩子的，只有悲哀；糊涂人的父亲，毫无乐趣。

text_en: A cheerful heart is a good medicine, but a downcast spirit dries up the bones.
text_cn: 愉快的心，是良好的治疗；神志忧郁，能使筋骨枯萎。

text_en: The wicked accept a concealed bribe to pervert the ways of justice.
text_cn: 恶人在大衣下受贿赂，是为颠倒正义的判词。

text_en: The discerning person looks to wisdom, but the eyes of a fool to the ends of the earth.
text_cn: 精明的人，常面向智慧；愚者的眼，向地极呆望，

text_en: Foolish children are a grief to their father and bitterness to her who bore them.
text_cn: 愚昧的儿子，是他父亲的痛苦，是他生母的忧伤。

text_en: To impose a fine on the innocent is not right, or to flog the noble for their integrity.
text_cn: 科罚无辜，已属不当；杖责君子，更属不义。

text_en: One who spares words is knowledgeable; one who is cool in spirit has understanding.
text_cn: 智者必沉默寡言，达人必心神镇定。

text_en: Even fools who keep silent are considered wise; when they close their lips, they are deemed intelligent.
text_cn: 愚人不发言，亦可充作智者；若谨口慎言，亦可视为哲人。
